newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh and tribal rebels hold peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh and tribal rebels hold peace talks.

text.p: Government and rebel leaders on Wednesday opened talks in an effort to end a decades-old insurgency in Bangladesh's southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts, officials said.
They said the two sides would continue their talks on Thursday in an attempt to reach consensus.
A team of leaders of the rebel Shanti Bahini (peace force), led by Jyotirindra Budhipriya Larma, flew to the capital for their second meeting with government leaders since January.
A senior parliamentary official of the ruling Awami League, Abud Hasanat Abdullah, heads the government side at the talks.

The Shanti Bahini has fought a bush war in the 5,500 sq-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts, bordering India and Burma, over demands for political autonomy and expulsion of about 500,000 Bengali-speaking settlers from the area.
Over 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency, according to official figures.

Bangladesh's main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party, led by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, and the fundamentalist Jamaat-e-Islami called for strikes in the Hill districts to protest against the peace talks.
The opposition criticises the government for jeopardising the interests of the Bengali settlers, who constitute about 49 percent of the total hill population.
